title: Unity by Claude Code with Gemini + Codex MCP + Unity MCP
author: Wide-Ad9537
selftext:
I did not know how to code c# but got on account trails for unlimited Opus 4.5 for a week with 3 hours reset limit.  , gemini and codex are just plus account . 
I try to create 2D games , where should I start? 
I was ask chat GPT for create RPD but Claude Code keep running into errors to errors , so any one could help me get clear vision how to start to end ? Like a baby please ?

comments.author: CulturalFig1237
comments.body: AI errors happen because the model does not understand your project context. Humans need fundamentals so they can fix and guide it.

comments.author: moneydollarz
comments.body: I highly suggest using Claude ai Sonnet 4.5 instead of Opus, also try LLMArena, you can use all the models for free without any limits. I suggest asking the ai to give you instructions on each step when creating your game that’s what I usually do

comments.author: Mustafag91
comments.body: There's Bezi AI specific for gamedev, as they say you can integrate it with the editor and it has context of your project, unlike other models. It understands your structure, design docs, etc.

replies.author: Other-Football72
replies.body: Have you used it? I was wondering what tier of plan makes sense for someone wanting maybe 1-4 hours a day of tinkering

replies.author: Mustafag91
replies.body: Nah I didn't, yet. Still learning C# and Unity lol. But saw Thomas Brush showcasing it. It has a free plan but don't know how flexible is that.

comments.author: spoie1
comments.body:
Do small bits at a time, expect to bug fix and scrap them later, test heavily, and *learn*.
Make sure you know what each line does and how it works, learn basic principles, and double check. Do not trust the LLM, use it as a tool 😅

I had very basic C#, but a very non-standard game to make, so have learnt *a lot* (was using UnityAssistant until they limited it as of a few days ago!), but have spent a lot of time bashing my head against a desk when it was plain wrong. I've learnt a lot looking at the code of assets too, as many tutorials are very narrow and specific 😅

Mostly, I'm writing my own now unless it's something I've not come across and need ideas for, 3 months in.

comments.author: Other-Football72
comments.body:
https://www.sololearn.com/en/learn/courses/coding-foundations

I have a minor background in coding, some Python and years ago C++, but just take the beginner course in C#, that will take 1 day. Then jump into the intermediate and pick the spots you may need, you can skip a lot.

Learn the basics, at the very least.
